record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop more general methods for quotienting out or breaking important symmetries, such as gauge symmetry, supersymmetry, and replica symmetry, together with a general theory of non-perturbative Ward identities.

evidence.quote: Many difficult constructive problems involve symmetries which are crucial to their understanding (gauge symmetries, supersymmetry, replica symmetry). One would like to have more general methods to quotient out or break these symmetries, and develop a more general theory of non-perturbative Ward identities.

artifact.category_tag: non-perturbative Ward identities and symmetry quotienting
artifact.status_search_result: This is a programmatic open problem in constructive quantum field theory: developing general non-perturbative tools for handling gauge, super-, and replica symmetries, and a general theory of non-perturbative Ward identities. While specific instances have been addressed (e.g., non-perturbative Ward identities in 2D models by Benfatto–Mastropietro and in QED-like models, and rigorous SUSY treatments in random band matrix and reinforced random walk contexts by Disertori–Spencer–Zirnbauer and others), no general framework exists, and the problem is widely regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Non-perturbative Ward identities (Benfatto–Mastropietro)
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous derivation of Ward identities for 1D and 2D interacting fermion systems via constructive renormalization group, in specific models.
status_evidence.claim: Non-perturbative Ward identities are established only in specific low-dimensional models, not as a general theory.

status_evidence.title: Disertori–Spencer–Zirnbauer, SUSY hyperbolic sigma model
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous analysis of a supersymmetric sigma model used for random band matrices, illustrating model-specific non-perturbative SUSY techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Constructive treatments of supersymmetry remain model-specific rather than part of a general framework.
